title: Acronis report says AI is helping some attackers compress the cyberattack lifecycle
date_note: SecurityBrief Australia gives only its publication day; no earlier day is stated.
geo_basis: no place stated in the source
summary: Acronis's Threat Research Unit published its first TRU Cyber Pulse 2026 report. It says artificial intelligence is helping some attackers compress the cyberattack lifecycle, and that AI-assisted attackers can move from newly disclosed vulnerabilities to weaponised exploits within hours. It also reports rising attacks on Linux and VMware ESXi systems.
plain: Acronis's new threat report says AI is helping some attackers speed up their attacks, moving from a newly disclosed flaw to a working exploit within hours.
exec: Acronis says AI-assisted attackers can weaponise newly disclosed vulnerabilities within hours, so patch windows may be shorter.

validation.note: Only SecurityBrief Australia read (the same article appears on sister sites of one publisher); Acronis's own report was not read.

evidence.quote: AI-assisted attackers can move from newly disclosed vulnerabilities to weaponised exploits within hours.
